subject.title: feat: keep reset session history searchable

question: Should `/reset` permanently change from an archive-and-remove boundary to a retained, searchable SQLite-history boundary, with physical disk pressure as the ordinary reclamation mechanism?
rationale: This is an intentional compatibility-sensitive change to core reset semantics and durable user/session state; code review can identify implementation defects but cannot decide the intended long-term product contract.

options.title: Accept durable reset history
options.body: Retain the new reset semantics after fixing budget enforcement gaps and documenting the upgrade behavior.

options.title: Preserve reset deletion semantics
options.body: Keep reset as archive-and-remove behavior and limit durable history retention to an explicit, separately designed feature.

options.title: Defer for a narrower design
options.body: Pause this large lifecycle change until the retention contract, archive classes, and pressure behavior are approved together.

recommendation.title: Accept durable reset history
recommendation.body: Retain the new reset semantics after fixing budget enforcement gaps and documenting the upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The available merged-history evidence connects steipete to the immediately preceding reset-policy decision and the proposed follow-on design.
